kalangala-oil-palm.conditions_add: The lender of record is IFAD, not the World Bank, and the money that paid for the Bugala Island estate was the first phase of the Vegetable Oil Development Project, a US$20 million IFAD loan approved in April 1997, effective in July 1998 and closed in December 2011; IFAD's interim evaluation of that phase names no covenant of the loan, and says the 24 risk-mitigation conditions on the oil palm development were set by Uganda's environment agency when it approved the 2003 environmental impact statement, not by the lender. The terms that are documented belong to the second phase, SDR 33.5 million (about US$52 million) put to IFAD's Executive Board on 21-22 April 2010: as conditions precedent to withdrawal IFAD had to accept the appointed project manager and financial controller, the agriculture ministry had to set up a contracts committee with delegated authority over procurement, and draft guidelines for oilseeds and oil palm development and a project operations and financial management manual had to be submitted to IFAD. A covenant of that second loan states that "No new oil palm development shall be undertaken on the outlying islands or Buvuma Island" until environmental impact assessments were carried out and the environment agency had issued its compliance certificate, and spending on the outlying islands and on the oilseed guarantee fund was eligible only "subject to prior approval by the Fund" (IFAD, EB 2010/99/R.19).

why.admin: a project operations and financial management manual had to be submitted to IFAD
why.safeguard: No new oil palm development shall be undertaken on the outlying islands or Buvuma Island
why.fincov: subject to prior approval by the Fund

libya-coast-guard-eu-italy-detention.conditions_add: The European Commission's action document for the EU Trust Fund programme "Support to Integrated Border and Migration Management in Libya" (EUR 42,223,927.28 of an estimated total cost of EUR 46.3 million, to Italy's Ministry of the Interior under indirect management, reference Ares(2019)7307599) makes parts of the money conditional. For the southern border activity it states that "The financing and completion of the activity will be conditional to the results of such assessment", and it states that "The financing of border control facilities will be also conditional to a progressive access of humanitarian actors". It also records that "The Libyan authorities have to commit not to move the personnel, once they are trained, to a different office/body", requires the Italian ministry to produce a progress report every four months including a conflict sensitivity analysis, and says regular assessments "will constitute a basis for a possible decision of suspension of activities".

why.fincov: The financing of border control facilities will be also conditional to a progressive access of humanitarian actors
why.admin: requires the Italian ministry to produce a progress report every four months including a conflict sensitivity analysis

NTPC, the Pakri-Barwadih mine, coal and power are not mentioned. Blank upheld.

The Accountability Console holds the Independent Recourse Mechanism complaint record only. World Bank documents for the fourth bridge resettlement plan exist on documents1.worldbank.org, but the World Bank is a different lender from the one named in this case. AfDB publishes no loan agreement, and its appraisal reports are not mirrored on any host that serves - checked africanwaterfacility.org and ecgnet.org, which serve but hold only other projects' reports. Spot-checked 11 November 2026 and the stated reason was corrected: the Early Warning System record for AFDB-P-CI-D00-010 does carry a project description taken from the bank's website, so the phrase "No project information available at the time of disclosure" does not apply to it. What the record does not carry is any condition: it gives a voting date of 16 October 2018 and US$202.00 million in investment and project cost, lists consultancy topics including road safety and environmental protection awareness, states no covenant or resettlement requirement, and links to no bank document beyond the AfDB project page. Blank upheld on the substance.

thwake-dam-makueni.searched: The mirror does hold one Thwake file, and it is not a financing document. https://ewsdata.rightsindevelopment.org/files/documents/17/AFDB-P-KE-E00-017.pdf fetched in full and is the borrower's Stakeholder Engagement Plan of May 2025: it restates AfDB's Integrated Safeguards System operational safeguards OS1 and OS5 as policy and says a Resettlement Action Plan will be disclosed, but sets no condition of the loan and post-dates the 2017 harm. The Early Warning System record for the additional financing (AFDB-P-KE-EA0-006, approved 14 November 2018) states "No project information available at the time of disclosure" and links only to afdb.org, which refuses. No appraisal report or loan agreement for the 2013 African Development Fund package is published anywhere that serves. Spot-checked 11 November 2026: the Early Warning System record for AFDB-P-KE-EA0-006 was opened and does say "No project information available at the time of disclosure", with a voting date of 14 November 2018, an investment amount of US$117.70 million, no condition or covenant of any kind, and no document link other than back to afdb.org. Blank upheld.

vares-adriatic-metals.searched: ebrd.com refuses and no mirror carries an EBRD financing document. Confirmed again this round: the Early Warning System mirrors ADB, AIIB, World Bank, AfDB and IDB files as PDFs but not EBRD's, and its EBRD records give only amount, instrument, board date and risk category with a link back to ebrd.com. For the GBP 6.2 million equity subscription in Adriatic Metals of 6 October 2020, an equity placement carries no use-of-proceeds covenant that any public source records, and EBRD's own statement that the money paid for studies rather than mine construction is reported second-hand through IPAM rather than in a bank document.

shah-deniz-sangachal.searched: ebrd.com refuses and no mirror carries an EBRD financing document. Confirmed again this round: the Early Warning System mirrors ADB, AIIB, World Bank, AfDB and IDB files as PDFs but not EBRD's, and its EBRD records give only amount, instrument, board date and risk category with a link back to ebrd.com. The US$500 million loan was to Lukoil as a corporate borrower, not to the Shah Deniz 2 project or the Sangachal terminal, so even a published covenant would be a term of a different loan from the one that built the works complained of.

ipp4-al-manakher-easep-detention.searched: ebrd.com refuses and no mirror carries an EBRD financing document. Confirmed again this round: the Early Warning System mirrors ADB, AIIB, World Bank, AfDB and IDB files as PDFs but not EBRD's, and its EBRD records give only amount, instrument, board date and risk category with a link back to ebrd.com. The 2012 US$100 million loan has no project summary document on any host that serves, and the co-lender's record (the US Overseas Private Investment Corporation) publishes no financing terms for IPP4 either.

naga-cebu-kepco-coal-dust.searched: ADB document paths do fetch, but the document that would carry the covenants does not exist. This was a non-sovereign private-sector loan, for which ADB publishes no Report and Recommendation of the President, no project data sheet of the usual kind and no facility agreement. Searches of adb.org project documents for the Visayas Base-Load Power Development Project, Naga, Cebu and KEPCO-SPC return only the technical assistance completion report and its Independent Evaluation Department validation (project 46947-012, on air quality monitoring capacity), which was read this round and mentions no loan covenant, no loan agreement and not the plant itself. The Compliance Review Panel's own reports for the complaint are not on any path that serves, and the Accountability Console record carries no financing term.

poland-nowa-huta-1988.searched: Settled as a finding rather than a failure, and re-stated here so it is not searched again: the World Bank documents API serves and returns no adjustment-lending document for Poland around 1988-1990. Poland joined the Bank and the Fund in June 1986 and Bank adjustment lending began only after the 1989 change of government, so there is no 1988 loan or programme whose conditions could bear on the Nowa Huta strike. The price reform of 1987-88 was the Polish government's own, adopted in the hope of later debt relief, which is not a lender condition.

eacop-bank-protest-arrests.searched: The lenders are commercial and regional banks and no facility agreement is published. BankTrack serves and gives the tranche structure - Standard Bank, Stanbic Bank Uganda and KCB Bank Uganda at US$200 million each, Afreximbank and the Islamic Corporation for the Development of the Private Sector at US$200 million each, and a US$100 million Islamic facility from the Islamic Development Bank - sourced to IJGlobal, but no covenant, condition precedent or security term. The Islamic Development Bank's project records give amounts only. There is no accountability-mechanism file for this financing to read instead.

messok-dja-baka-ecoguards.searched: Read the right document and it says the requirements were policy, not terms of the money. UNDP's SECU final investigation report (SECU0009, on info.undp.org, which serves) attributes the screening, Indigenous Peoples Plan and free, prior and informed consent requirements to UNDP's own Social and Environmental Standards, and states at paragraph 23 that "UNDP is not required to ensure compliance with the SES of activities that are not funded through UNDP accounts". It records that the project document makes no reference to those standards and that no Indigenous Peoples Plan was prepared, and it describes the UNDP-WWF letters of agreement as carrying delivery indicators such as patrol and arrest counts, not safeguard conditions. The Global Environment Facility grant's own terms are not published and the report names none.

guatemala-std-inoculation-1946.searched: Not a loan and no agreement exists to read. The money was a 1946-48 US Public Health Service research grant routed through the Pan American Sanitary Bureau to Guatemalan ministries; the US government's own accounts of the episode describe the funding route but publish no grant instrument, and no condition attached to the grant is recorded anywhere. Nothing new was tried on the document routes named in the brief because none of them covers 1940s US bilateral research grants.

somsanga-drug-detention-laos.searched: The funding was a series of small bilateral and UN agency grants - US$145,786 for a clinic, a US$95,200 renovation, US$22,500, US$10,000 and US$9,300 contributions - and no grant agreement or funding instrument for any of them is published, so there is no document in which a condition could appear. The US State Department, UNODC, Japanese, Singaporean, German and Australian records that describe the payments give purposes and amounts only.

choam-chao-unicef-youth-centre.searched: UNICEF gave unspecified "limited funding" through Cambodia's Ministry of Social Affairs and publishes no grant agreement or amount for the Choam Chao centre, so there is no instrument whose terms could be reported. UNICEF's own account states only that it supported the centre from 2006 and stopped funding after confirming abuse reports, which is a withdrawal rather than a condition.

desert-dumps-eu-north-africa.searched: A conditions document was found but it belongs to a different EU action. The EU action document for the Multi-Country Migration Programme for the Southern Neighbourhood (CRIS NDICI-GEO-NEAR/2021/043-487, EUR 45 million, of which EUR 25 million for Tunisia), released by Statewatch and read in full this round, does set terms: "The action can only be implemented with persons who are not on the sanctions list", only EU-based partners may deliver the equipment and training to prevent its misuse, and it states that it is "not envisaged to conclude a financing agreement with the partner countries". But that money funds a maritime training academy, a rescue coordination centre and coastal surveillance in Tunisia, not the EU Trust Fund money for migration management that this case describes, and it covers Libya and Tunisia only, not Morocco or Mauritania. Attaching it here would be a term from a different grant, so the case is left blank; the next round can use it if the case's scope is widened.

unicef-tube-wells-bangladesh-arsenic.searched: UNICEF worked with Bangladesh's Department of Public Health Engineering to install tube-wells from the 1970s under a grant programme for which no agreement, amount or funding instrument is published, and the account of its role comes from a WHO Bulletin article rather than a funding document. There is no document in which a condition on the money could be recorded, and the private suppliers who installed most of the later wells had no UNICEF funding at all.

virunga-eu-rangers-residents.searched: Read the EU's own announcement of the grant and it carries no term. The European Commission's capacity4dev page for the EUR 53 million grant signed on 28 November 2016 between the EU, the DRC government and the Virunga Foundation (of which EUR 15.4 million comes from the 11th European Development Fund national indicative programme) states the purpose and the five-year term and nothing about conditions, obligations on the foundation or the government, spending restrictions, reporting or oversight. The contribution agreement itself is not published, and no EU action document for the grant could be found.
